Furthermore, the claim presents a definition that is not found in the text; the text uses $n$ as a parameter for calculation without defining its semantic meaning as 'side length'.

Multi-pass Projection Voxelization, also known as Primitive Voxelization, was introduced in the paper "A GPU-based voxelization approach to 3D Minkowski sum computation" [S1].

The evidence explicitly states in Section 4.1 that the authors use a technique called 'Primitive Voxelization' (or 'primitive voxelization') as the first step of their algorithm. The description of this technique in the evidence matches the claim: it involves projecting surfaces onto a 2D plane, rasterizing them, mapping fragments to voxels, using a 3D texture, rendering multiple times (using MRT), and addressing perpendicular surfaces by projecting along three orthogonal directions and compositing the results. The claim that this is also known as 'Multi-pass Projection Voxelization' is consistent with the evidence describing the multi-pass nature (rendering the VBO multiple times, composing three directional voxelizations).
